newsitem.title: UK: Large UK multinationals targeted by tax change.
newsitem.headline: Large UK multinationals targeted by tax change.

text.p: A small number of large multinational companies are the target of UK budget measures announced on Tuesday to prevent a method of tax avoidance, tax experts said.

The UK's Inland Revenue said in a statement the measure to "prevent UK based companies using artificial schemes involving overseas companies to reduce their tax bills" would bring "around 50 million stg per year...and safeguards the Exchequer from a potentially much greater loss of tax".

Kevin Phillips, corporate tax partner at international accountancy firm Ernst & Young, said schemes under which a UK company claims credit for foreign tax paid by an unconnected overseas company to reduce its own UK tax, were rare.
He said the measure was targeted at "a very specialised scheme" although for the companies involved "there could be substantial amounts at stake."
Only a handful of companies were prepared to enter into such schemes, which involved companies "buying in" highly taxed foreign income, reducing their UK tax exposure, he added.
